caption:
After maxillary sinus augmentation with autogenous bone alone, graft volume dropped by about 42% within 6 months. In a split-mouth CT study of 10 patients with bilateral sinus augmentation, one side received autogenous bone only and the other a mixture of hydroxyapatite and autogenous bone (80:20). Between day 15 and day 180, volume decreased by 42.3% with autogenous bone and by 25.9% with the mixture. Both sides still gained bone for implant placement. Note: small sample of 10 patients.

Source: Cosso MG, de Brito RB Jr, Piattelli A, Shibli JA, Zenóbio EG. Volumetric dimensional changes of autogenous bone and the mixture of hydroxyapatite and autogenous bone graft in humans maxillary sinus augmentation. A multislice tomographic study. Clin Oral Implants Res. 2014;25(11):1251-1256. doi:10.1111/clr.12261. PMID 24102867
